t: Largest Number After Mutating Substring -- One Greedy Mutation Window
o: You may pick one contiguous substring of num and replace every digit d inside it by change[d]; mutating nothing is also allowed. Because every candidate keeps the same length, comparing results is ordinary left-to-right digit comparison decided at the first differing position. In Example 1 ("132" with mappings 1->8, 3->0, 2->5) mutating just the leading 1 yields "832"; extending through the 3 would force 3->0 and produce "805", which is worse despite the later 2->5 gain. In Example 2 ("021") every mapping grows its digit, so the whole string mutates to "934". In Example 3 ("5" with 5->2) no digit improves, so the original stands. With num up to 10^5 digits, a single linear scan is the target.
k: Same-length numbers compare lexicographically, so the winning strategy upgrades the leftmost digit that can be upgraded.
Once a digit inside the window would shrink (change[d] < d), the substring must stop there -- one loss at any included position outweighs every later gain.
Digits with change[d] == d are neutral and can sit inside the mutated window freely.

a.i: Enumerate every candidate substring [i, j], apply the mapping to a working copy, and keep the best string seen. This mirrors the definition directly and is easy to trust, but it touches O(n^2) substrings with O(n) construction each.
s: Start with the original string as the best answer.
For every start i, extend an end j from i onward, mapping digit num[j] into a working copy each step.
Compare each candidate against the best and keep the larger.
a.t: O(n^3) character work -- O(n^2) candidates, each built and compared in O(n)
a.sp: O(n) -- one working copy plus the best string

a.i: Locate the first digit the mapping enlarges (change[d] > d); upgrading the most significant improvable digit dominates every alternative. From that index keep mutating while mappings are non-shrinking (change[d] >= d), and cut the window the moment a digit would shrink -- reaching anything beyond would require swallowing that loss at an earlier, higher-weight position.
s: Advance i while change[digit] <= digit (nothing to gain yet).
Mutate consecutive digits while change[digit] >= digit, writing mapped digits back.
Stop at the first shrinking digit or the end of the string.
a.t: O(n) -- each digit is examined a constant number of times
a.sp: O(n) -- one mutable copy of the digit string (O(1) extra where strings are edited in place)

w: Go straight to the greedy in an interview; keep the brute force only as a mental checker for tiny inputs. Pitfalls: opening the window demands strict improvement (change[d] > d) but staying inside it only demands no shrinkage (change[d] >= d) -- conflating the two breaks cases like "132". If no digit ever improves, return the original untouched. Edge cases: all-shrinking mappings and leading zeros (permitted, since the input itself may contain them). Follow-ups to expect: at most k disjoint mutated substrings, or forced mutation -- both reuse the same leftmost-gain reasoning.
